en.title: Spider-Man's $355M Debut Knocks The Odyssey Off Box Office Throne
en.summary: The latest webslinger adventure has arrived with a bang, dethroning a critical darling and shattering box office records. It's a monumental opening weekend for Marvel's hero.
en.body:
The summer movie season has a new king. **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** has officially swung into the top spot at the box office, unseating Christopher Nolan's critically acclaimed epic, **The Odyssey**. In its opening weekend, the latest Marvel Cinematic Universe installment, starring **Tom Holland**, raked in a staggering $355 million domestically. This colossal debut not only makes it the highest-grossing film of 2026 but also secures its place as the second-biggest opening weekend in box office history, a feat that brings it incredibly close to the all-time record held by **Avengers: Endgame**.

The combined box office power of **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** and **The Odyssey** has also set a new benchmark, marking the biggest collective box office weekend ever. While **The Odyssey** has now moved to second place after two dominant weekends, it's hardly a defeat. Nolan's historical drama continues to perform exceptionally well, pulling in $51 million in its third weekend alone, demonstrating remarkable staying power in a landscape often dominated by franchise fare. Its extended 70mm IMAX run is set to continue through mid-September, ensuring it remains a significant draw for audiences seeking a premium theatrical experience.

## A New Era for Blockbusters

The success of **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** is a testament to the franchise's global appeal. The film grossed an additional $572 million internationally in its opening weekend, pushing its worldwide total to an astonishing $927 million. This nearly reaches the coveted billion-dollar mark within its first three days, a rare achievement that underscores the immense anticipation and dedicated fanbase that turned out in droves. This performance solidifies **Spider-Man**'s position as one of the most bankable characters in cinema history and a crucial anchor for Sony Pictures' cinematic universe.

Meanwhile, **Toy Story 5** continues its own triumphant run, having already surpassed the $1 billion mark globally. The animated sequel holds steady in third place, cementing its status as another major summer success story. Family-friendly titles like **Minions & Monsters** and **Moana** are also finding their audiences, capitalizing on the summer break. Even **Hadestown: The Musical** has extended its limited run, adding a respectable $2 million to its tally, proving that diverse theatrical offerings can still thrive.

## What This Means for Fans

For **Spider-Man** fans, this opening weekend is a massive celebration. The film's near-record-breaking debut suggests that the appetite for well-crafted superhero narratives remains as strong as ever, especially when delivered with the action, heart, and humor that the **Spider-Man** franchise is known for. The intense competition at the top of the box office also benefits audiences, offering a rich selection of high-quality films across different genres. The fact that **Tom Holland** is also enjoying a double feature, with **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** dominating and **The Odyssey** holding its ground, is a testament to a robust and diverse cinematic landscape.

## What's Next

**Spider-Man: Brand New Day** is now playing in theaters worldwide. Some digital IMAX screens will transition to feature the film starting August 6th. **The Odyssey** will continue its exclusive 70mm IMAX engagements into mid-September.

content_raw: After two record-breaking weekends at the top of the box office, The Odyssey has conceded the top spot to a new suitor, the latest Marvel entry from Sony Pictures, Spider-Man: Brand New Day . The Hollywood Reporter noted the Tom Holland-led sequel was just a webshot away from besting Avengers: Endgame ‘s record domestic opening of $357.1 million back in 2019. Swinging into second place with just $2 million short of a pre-pandemic theatrical record is no easy feat, as the moviegoing landscape has seen many changes in the last six years. Globally, our friendly neighborhood Spider-Man netted another hefty $572 million, landing the franchise just short of the billion-dollar mark at $927 million in its opening weekend.  Don’t feel too bad for Odysseus and his crew just yet. Nolan’s big Hollywood epic has plenty of staying power, holding steady with a $51 million draw in its third weekend. Plus, if you’re still waiting to get a chance (or another chance) to see The Odyssey in 70mm IMAX, the unprecedented run will continue into mid-September, while some digital IMAX screens will move over to give Spider-Man: Brand New Day a belated big screen run starting August 6, according to Variety .  Disney’s Toy Story 5 is the summer’s other big box office success story. Last week, it crossed the $1 billion dollar mark and held down the third spot just after Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey with an additional $6 million for the year’s highest grossing film so far. Other family-friendly titles like Minions & Monsters and Moana are finding audiences while their young target demo is out for the summer. Hadestown: The Musical extended its original limited five-day run to add $2 million to its tally. Holland isn’t the only actor enjoying a double feature in the top box office charts, as Olivia Wilde’s adult comedy The Invite holds the 7th spot for another weekend, followed by Gregg Araki’s kinky comedy I Want Your Se x, which debuted with $600,000 in its first weekend.
